rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the command to mean exalting the Lord above what idol worshippers say.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : عظم ربك / مما يقوله عبدة الأوثان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the command is to say “God is greatest”; a report adds that the Prophet said it when the verse came, and Khadija rejoiced and recognized revelation.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : هو أن يقول : الله أكبر ، روى أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may mean saying the takbir in prayer; although obligatory prayer had not yet been instituted, the Prophet could have had voluntary prayers.
rows.anchor: المراد منه التكبير في الصلوات ، فإن قيل : هذه السورة نزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After “arise and warn,” the command may mean declaring the Lord above idle talk and frivolity.
rows.anchor: لما قيل له : { قم فأنذر } قيل بعد ذلك : { وربك فكبر } عن اللغو والعبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is to exalt God above partners, opposites, equals, and likeness to contingent created things; knowing and declaring God's transcendence precedes other calls.
rows.anchor: أن يكبر ربه عن الشركاء والأضداد والأنداد ومشابهة الممكنات والمحدثات

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
rows.claim: Abu al-Fath al-Mawsili treats the fāʾ as extra, as in “Zayd, then strike” meaning simply “strike Zayd.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفتح الموصلي : يقال : زيدا فاضرب ، وعمرا فاشكر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the fāʾ conveys a consequence: rise and therefore magnify your Lord, and the following commands work similarly.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : دخلت الفاء لإفادة معنى الجزائية ، والمعنى : قم فكبر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf author reads the fāʾ conditionally: whatever happens, do not cease magnifying God.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الفاء لإفادة معنى الشرط ، والتقدير : وأي شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To think or reflect is to examine and deliberate over a matter.
rows.anchor: فكر في الأمر وتفكر إذا نظر فيه وتدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reflecting, he arranged words in his heart and prepared them; this is what “he determined” means.
rows.anchor: ثم لما تفكر رتب في قلبه كلاما وهيأه وهو المراد من قوله : { فقدر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula is used for amazement and magnification, as in proverbial curses that exclaim how courageous or eloquent someone is.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنما يذكر عند التعجب والاستعظام ، ومثله قولهم : قتله الله ما أشجعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading marvels at the strength of his thinking: he could not have devised a stronger or greater doubt against Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أنه تعجيب من قوة خاطره ، يعني أنه لا يمكن القدح في أمر محمد عليه السلام بشبهة أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is sarcastic praise: what he proposed was extremely feeble and worthless.
rows.anchor: الثناء عليه على طريقة الاستهزاء ، يعني أن هذا الذي ذكره في غاية الركاكة والسقوط

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth distinguishes facial states: ʿabasa is furrowing the brow; showing teeth while frowning is kalaḥ; brooding and thinking is basara; anger added to that is basala.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : عبس يعبس فهو عابس إذا قطب ما بين عينيه ، فإن أبدى عن أسنانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away from the rest of the people toward his family, and arrogantly refused to believe.
rows.anchor: أدبر عن سائر الناس إلى أهله واستكبر أي تعظم عن الإيمان

words: فَقَالَ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌۭ يُؤْثَرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks immediate sequence: after turning away in pride, he voiced this objection.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكره بفاء التعقيب ليعلم أنه لما ولى واستكبر ذكر هذه الشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense is that the magic is related as a story passed down from earlier people; the root usage is reporting after them.
rows.anchor: أثرت الحديث آثره أثرا إذا حدثت به عن قوم في آثارهم ، أي بعدما ماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means that this is preferred above all magic, from the verb for preferring one thing over another.
rows.anchor: الثاني : يؤثر على جميع السحر ، وعلى هذا يكون هو من الإيثار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take “spare” and “leave” as synonyms repeated for emphasis, like saying “he turned me away and avoided me.”
rows.anchor: فمنهم من قال : هما لفظان مترادفان معناهما واحد ، والغرض من التكرير التأكيد

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through ʿAta says the fire leaves no blood, flesh, or bone; when they are recreated it burns them more intensely again, repeatedly.
rows.anchor: وهذا رواية عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another distinction: it leaves no person deserving punishment without torment, then leaves no part of those bodies unburned.
rows.anchor: ثانيها : لا تبقي من المستحقين للعذاب إلا عذبتهم ، ثم لا تذر

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A further distinction is that the fire leaves no body part, and uses all its power and intensity in tormenting them.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : لا تبقي من أبدان المعذبين شيئا ، ثم إن تلك النيران لا تذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are in gardens whose qualities cannot be fully encompassed.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { في جنات } أي هم في جنات لا يكتنه وصفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse treats “about” as an extra particle: they ask the criminals directly, “What brought you into Saqar?”
rows.anchor: أن تكون كلمة عن صلة زائدة ، والتقدير : يتساءلون المجرمين

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Alternatively, the people of the right ask one another about the criminals; al-Kashshaf answers that the criminals recount what happened between them and the questioners.
rows.anchor: أجاب صاحب ( الكشاف ) عنه فقال : المراد من هذا أن المسؤولين يلقون إلى السائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that the people of the right asked where the criminals were, then addressed them when they saw them.
rows.anchor: وفيه وجه آخر ، وهو أن يكون المراد أن أصحاب اليمين كانوا يتساءلون عن المجرمين أين هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many implicit elements in the exchange exemplify how often the Qur'an leaves material understood from context.
rows.anchor: والإضمارات كثيرة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question adds rebuke and humiliation; it asks what detained them in this depth of the Fire.
rows.anchor: المقصود من السؤال زيادة التوبيخ والتخجيل ، والمعنى ما حبسكم في هذه الدركة من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The failures to pray and feed the poor mean neglect of obligatory prayer and zakat, since people cannot be punished for omitting non-obligatory acts.
rows.anchor: وهذان يجب أن يكونا محمولين على الصلاة الواجبة ، والزكاة الواجبة لأن ما ليس بواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their joining those who “delved” means engaging in falsehoods.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : { وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين } والمراد منه الأباطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “certainty” that finally came to them means death; they denied the resurrection until dying.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : { وكنا نكذب بيوم الدين } أي بيوم القيامة حتى أتانا اليقين ، أي الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording apparently says that each member of those groups possessed all four listed traits.
rows.anchor: وظاهر اللفظ يدل على أن كل أحد من أولئك الأقوام كان موصوفا بهذه الخصال الأربعة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author's school cites this verse to argue that unbelievers are punished for neglecting the subsidiary rules of religious law; he says the detailed treatment is in al-Mahsul.
rows.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن الكفار يعذبون بترك فروع الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although denial of judgment is the worst fault, it comes last to stress that they persisted in it after the preceding three traits.
rows.anchor: أريد أنهم بعد اتصافهم بتلك الأمور الثلاثة كانوا مكذبين بيوم الدين ، والغرض تعظيم هذا الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder they turn away from is admonition, whether the Qur'an or other exhortations.
rows.anchor: أي عن الذكر وهو العظة يريد القرآن أو غيره من المواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Turning away” is accusative as a circumstantial expression, like “what is the matter with you, standing?”
rows.anchor: ومعرضين نصب على الحال كقولهم مالك قائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their aversion to the Qur'an is likened to frightened wild asses fleeing from a pursuer.
rows.anchor: ثم شبههم في نفورهم عن القرآن بحمر نافرة فقال : ! 7 { كأنهم حمر مستنفرة * فرت من قسورة }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the asses as wild asses and explains mustanfira as fleeing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد الحمر الوحشية ، ومستنفرة أي نافرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired forms nafar and istanfara can both mean taking fright, like the pairs sakira/istaskhara and ʿajiba/istaʿjaba.
rows.anchor: يقال : نفر واستنفر مثل سخر ، واستسخر ، وعجب واستعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fatḥa reading is also reported and understood as “made to flee,” the asses being driven into flight.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح ، وهي المنفرة المحمولة على النفار

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi prefers kasra because “fled from a qaswara” indicates that the asses themselves were startled.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : الكسر في مستنفرة أولى ألا ترى أنه قال : { فرت من قسورة }

rows.speaker: أبو سوار الغنوي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Sallam asked the eloquent Bedouin Abu Sawwar what kind of asses; he answered that they were mustanfira, driven by a qaswara, supporting the kasra reading.
rows.anchor: قال : سألت أبا سوار الغنوي ، وكان أعرابيا فصيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed meaning of qaswara is a lion; the word is linked to qasr, subjugation, since the lion overpowers beasts.
rows.anchor: أنها الأسد يقال : ليوث قساور ، وهي فعولة من القسر وهو القهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas compares idolaters fleeing Muhammad to wild asses fleeing when they see a lion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الحمر الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد هربت كذلك هؤلاء المشركين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara is the Ethiopian word for lion.
rows.anchor: ثم قال ابن عباس : القسورة ، هي الأسد بلسان الحبشة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima disagrees that this is the Ethiopian word for lion, saying that the Ethiopian word is ʿanbasa.
rows.anchor: وخالف عكرمة فقال : الأسد بلسان الحبشة ، عنبسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes qaswara as the group of archers who hunt the asses.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : القسورة ، جماعة الرماة الذين يتصيدونها

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says qaswara is a collective name for archers with no singular of the same form.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري : هو اسم جمع للرماة لا واحد له من جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed meanings of qaswara are the press and voices of people, or the darkness of night.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : القسورة : ركز الناس وأصواتهم ورابعها : أنها ظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the comparison brands them foolish: no flight is like wild asses' frantic running when afraid.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وفي تشبيههم بالحمر شهادة عليهم بالبله ، ولا ترى مثل نفار حمير الوحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demanded that each person receive a sky-sent book addressed to him by name and commanding him to follow the Messenger, paralleling another demand for a readable book from heaven.
rows.anchor: أنهم قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : لا نؤمن بك حتى تأتي كل واحد منا بكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says they wanted a written book on parchment that they could touch with their hands.
rows.anchor: ونظيره { لن نؤمن * لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرءه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some said they wanted each man to wake with a page declaring him safe from the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن كان محمد صادقا فليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءة من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also cited a report that an Israelite woke with his sin and its expiation written on his head; al-Razi says this is far from “pages spread out” unless that means openly displayed writing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يقولون بلغنا أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل كان يصبح مكتوبا على رأسه ذنبه وكفارته

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reads both words with the lighter forms, since spreading and causing to spread are equivalent, like the paired forms anzala/nazzala.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير { صحفا منشرة } بتخفيفهما على أن أنشر الصحف ونشرها واحد

none: The segment is a fragment containing only an opening brace.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No indeed” rebukes their demand for that special revelation and stops their proposing further signs.
rows.anchor: كلا } وهو ردع لهم عن تلك الإرادة ، وزجر عن اقتراح الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned from reflection because they do not fear the afterlife; the many miracles already sufficed to establish prophethood, so demanding more is obstinate.
rows.anchor: فلذلك أعرضوا عن التأمل ، فإنه لما حصلت المعجزات الكثيرة ، كفت في الدلالة على صحة النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke addresses their turning away from the reminder.
rows.anchor: كلا } وهو ردع لهم عن إعراضهم عن التذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a powerful, sufficient reminder; whoever wills may keep it before his eyes, and the benefit is his own.
rows.anchor: إنه تذكرة } يعني تذكرة بليغة كافية { فمن شاء ذكره } أي جعله نصب عينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in “it is a reminder” and “remember it” refer to the reminder in the earlier passage; the feminine marker reflects the sense of remembrance or Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { أنه } { * وذكره } للتذكرة في قوله : { الشافعين فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites interpret God's willing as compelling people and forcing them to remember.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : يعني إلا أن يقسرهم على الذكر ويلجئهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the coercive reading: remembrance is negated except when God wills it, so its absence shows that He did not will it; restricting the will to coercion departs from the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: والجواب : أنه تعالى نفى الذكر مطلقا ، واستثنى عنه حال المشيئة المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yadhakkarun is read with either yāʾ or tāʾ and in both lighter and doubled forms.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يذكرون بالياء والتاء مخففا ومشددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is worthy of His servants' reverent fear and obedience, and worthy to forgive their past unbelief when they believe and obey.
rows.anchor: هو حقيق بأن يتقيه عباده ويخافوا عقابه فيؤمنوا ويطيعوا وحقيق بأن يغفر لهم ما سلف من كفرهم إذا آمنوا وأطاعوا

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The investigators say an oath by these things is in reality an oath by their Lord and Creator, as if swearing by the Lord of Resurrection that it will occur.
rows.anchor: أن المحققين قالوا : القسم بهذه الأشياء قسم بربها وخالقها في الحقيقة ، فكأنه قيل : أقسم برب القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection about other divine oaths does not apply: those passages swear by created things, while this wording denies that God is swearing by these things themselves.
rows.anchor: وأما ههنا فإنه نفي كونه تعالى مقسما بهذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads “no indeed” as rebuking the Prophet's haste and urging deliberation; the ensuing address broadens the point to humanity, created hasty and therefore loving the present and abandoning the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { كلا } ردع لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عادة العجلة

rows.speaker: سائر المفسرين
rows.claim: Other commentators take kalla to mean “indeed”: indeed people love the immediate world, work for it, and turn away from the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال سائر المفسرين : { كلا } معناه حقا أي حقا تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains the t/y variants as shifts between direct address and speaking about the described people, as in the Qur'anic shift from “you were” to “they sailed.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : القرآن إذا نزل تعريفا لحال قوم ، فتارة ينزل على سبيل المخاطبة لهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says yāʾ follows the earlier mention of “the human,” meant collectively, while tāʾ is an implied command to tell them, “you love and leave.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : الياء على ما تقدم من ذكر الإنسان في قوله : { أيحسب الإنسان }

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes kalla as a rebuke against preferring worldly life: the afterlife's fates dwarf the world, and death ends the temporary life before the eternal one.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : كلا ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة ، كأنه قيل : لما عرفتم صفة سعادة السعداء

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others read kalla as “indeed”: when death arrives, worldly life necessarily ends and one tastes death's bitterness.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : { كلا } أي حقا إذا بلغت التراقي كان كذا وكذا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the unbeliever denies the resurrection but cannot deny that death and its pains must come.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : { كلا } أي لا يؤمن الكافر بما ذكر من أمر القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted subject of “reaches the collarbones” is the soul or spirit, understood by the audience; tarāqī is the paired collarbones between the throat hollow and shoulders.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : المراد إذا بلغت النفس أو الروح أخبر عما لم يجر له ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul reaching the collarbones is a euphemism for nearing death, as in Duraid ibn al-Simma's verse about lives reaching the collarbones.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه يكنى ببلوغ النفس التراقي عن القرب من الموت ، ومنه قول دريد بن الصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same nearness-to-death expression appears in the Qur'an as reaching the throat.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { وبلغت * الحلقوم } ( الأحزاب : 10 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A critic argues that the soul reaches the collarbones only after leaving the heart, which would mean death already occurred, although the passage still describes signs of life.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : قال بعض الطاعنين : إن النفس إنما تصل إلى التراقي بعد مفارقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers that the phrase means nearing that state, not fully reaching it, so it does not imply that life continues after death.
rows.anchor: والجواب : المراد من قوله : { حتى إذا * بلغت التراقي } أي إذا حصل القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suda means left without instruction, prohibition, duty, or accountability for one's deeds in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي مهملا لا يؤمر ، ولا ينهى ، ولا يكلف في الدنيا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi defines the word as neglected or left unattended, as when one lets camels loose.
rows.anchor: والسدي في اللغة المهمل يقال : أسديت إبلي إسداء أهملتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse returns to the opening question about whether God will gather human bones and supplies the first proof of resurrection: humans cannot have been given faculties without duties.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر في أول السورة ، قوله : { أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God gave power, instruments, and reason without commands to obey or prohibitions against evil, that would imply approval of vile acts, contrary to divine wisdom; therefore there must be moral duty.
rows.anchor: وتقريره أن إعطاء القدرة والآلة والعقل بدون التكليف والأمر بالطاعة والنهي عن المفاسد يقتضي كونه تعالى راضيا بقبائح الأفعال ، وذلك لا يليق بحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duty befits the gracious and merciful God only if there is an afterlife of reward and resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإذا لا بد من التكليف والتكليف لا يحسن ولا يليق بالكريم الرحيم إلا إذا كان هناك دار الثواب والبعث والقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses likewise connect the coming Hour and moral accountability, and distinguish believers from wrongdoers and the pious from sinners.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله : { إن الساعة ءاتية أكاد أخفيها لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى } ( طه : 15 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nutfa is a small amount of water, here a little fluid in the man's loins and the woman's ribs.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : النطفة هي الماء القليل وجمعها نطاف ونطف ، يقول : ألم يك ماء قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Poured” means ejaculated into the womb; the verb is also discussed at the cited verses about semen being emitted.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { من منى يمنى } أي يصب في الرحم ، وذكرنا الكلام في يمنى عند قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning that the semen is poured subtly recalls its lowly origin and the filthy outlet it passes through; a creature made from it should not rebel against God.
rows.anchor: قلنا : فيه إشارة إلى حقارة حاله ، كأنه قيل : إنه مخلوق من المني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowly bodily function is expressed indirectly, as when the Qur'an says Jesus and Mary ate food, alluding to their need to relieve themselves.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى في عيسى ومريم : { كانا يأكلان الطعام } ( المائدة : 75 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has a tāʾ reading with the feminine nutfa as subject (“is poured”), or a yāʾ reading with semen as subject, meaning man's creation is decreed from it.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثانية : في يمنى في هذه السورة قراءتان التاء والياء ، فالتاء للنطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From him” means from the human, and the two kinds are the two categories of people.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { فجعل منه } أي من الإنسان { الزوجين } يعني الصنفين

words: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْۦِىَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who originated these things is surely able to bring the dead back to life.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أليس ذلك الذي أنشأ هذه الأشياء بقادر على الإعادة ،

words: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْۦِىَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that when the Prophet recited this verse he said, “Glory to You; yes indeed, and praise belongs to God, Lord of all worlds.”
rows.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأها قال : سبحانك بلى والحمد لله رب العالمين

none: The segment quotes verse 76:23 but offers no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah begins by saying humans emerged after nonexistence and were created from mixtures; Razi lists possible mixtures as elements, humors, parental fluids, body and spirit, body and soul, or successive embryonic stages, all pointing to a freely choosing Creator.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه سبحانه بين في أول السورة أن الإنسان وجد بعد العدم بقوله : { هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings were not created in vain but for trial and examination.
rows.anchor: ثم بين بعد ذلك أني ما خلقته ضائعا عاطلا باطلا ، بل خلقته لأجل الابتلاء والامتحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplied hearing, sight, and reason for the trial, then singled out reason as the noblest faculty and said He guided the path.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى أني أعطيته جميع ما يحتاج إليه عند الابتلاء والامتحان ، وهو السمع والبصر والعقل

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: The division into grateful and ungrateful people is, on the Qadari reading, the result of their own choice.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإنقسام باختيارهم كما هو تأويل القدرية

rows.speaker: الجبرية
rows.claim: The Jabri reading attributes the division into grateful and ungrateful people to God.
rows.anchor: أو من الله على ما هو تأويل الجبرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah gives punishment briefly but reward at length; Razi says this signals that mercy is stronger and more prevalent.
rows.anchor: ذكر عذاب الكفار على الاختصار ، ثم ذكر بعد ذلك ثواب المطيعين على الاستقصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through “your striving is appreciated,” the surah treats the afterlife; it then shifts to worldly matters and puts the obedient before the rebellious.
rows.anchor: فظهر مما بينا أن السورة من أولها إلى هذا الموضع في بيان أحوال الآخرة ، ثم إنه تعالى شرع بعد ذلك في أحوال الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is addressed as the head of the obedient community; an introductory reassurance precedes commands and prohibitions to steady him, and prohibitions precede commands because removing harm takes priority over gaining benefit.
rows.anchor: والرسول هو الرأس والرئيس ، فلهذا خص الرسول بالخطاب . واعلم أن الخطاب إما النهي وإما الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's arrangement is excellent: its opening subject matter, reassurance, ordering of prohibitions before commands, and later treatment of rebels all fit together.
rows.anchor: ومن تأمل فيما ذكرناه علم أن هذه السورة ، وقعت على أحسن وجوه الترتيب والنظام

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَنزِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse steadies the Messenger and opens his heart amid accusations of soothsaying and magic: God confirms that the Qur'an is revelation from Him.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المقصود من هذه الآية تثبيت الرسول وشرح صدره فيما نسبوه إليه من كهانة وسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the pronoun after making it the subject intensifies confirmation: though the unbelievers call it soothsaying, God emphatically declares it true revelation and truthful sending from Him.
rows.anchor: فلا جرم بالغ وكرر الضمير بعد إيقاعه اسما ، لأن تأكيدا على تأكيد أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reassurance removes the loneliness caused by the unbelievers' attacks, since the Lord of the heavens honors and confirms the Messenger even if ignorant people slander him.
rows.anchor: إحداهما : إزالة الوحشة المتقدمة الحاصلة بسبب طعن أولئك الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also strengthens him for future duties: although he wanted to fight those who tormented him, God commands patience and postpones permission to fight according to the wisdom of revelation in stages.
rows.anchor: والثانية : تقويته على تحمل التكليف المستقبل ، وذلك لأن الكفار كانوا يبالغون في إيذائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was revealed gradually according to wisdom that assigns each matter its appointed time; the Messenger should patiently accept his Lord's wise, faultless decree.
rows.anchor: إني ما نزلت عليك هذا القرآن مفرقا منجما إلا لحكمة بالغة تقتضي تخصيص كل شيء بوقت معين
